subject: Animation
title: Follow Through and Overlapping Action
description: A micro-lesson that makes Follow Through and Overlapping Action usable.

hook.text: When a character stops running, their hair, clothes, and accessories keep moving. This is follow through.

buildup.text: Different body parts move at different speeds. Arms swing after the body stops. Ears flop after the head turns.

discovery.text: Overlapping action means not everything starts and stops at the same time, creating fluid, natural motion.

twist.text: Without follow through, characters look like rigid mannequins. It is the detail that makes animation feel real.

climax.text: Follow through and overlapping action turn simple movement into the rich, layered motion of real life.

punchline.text: In great animation, nothing stops all at once.

quiz.question: What is the difference between follow through and overlapping action?
options: They are the same thing with different names
Follow through is parts continuing after a stop; overlapping action is parts moving at different rates
Follow through is for fast motion; overlapping is for slow motion
